subject: Chemistry
title: Naming Haloalkanes and Haloarenes: Common and IUPAC Names
summary: Every halide has two correct names. The common name is the alkyl group + halide (isopropyl chloride, ethyl chloride). The IUPAC name writes the halogen as a prefix (fluoro, chloro, bromo, iodo) on the longest chain, numbered from the end that gives the lowest locants; when both ends tie, alphabetical order decides (2-bromo-3-methylbutane). On benzene one halogen keeps the same name (chlorobenzene); two use o-, m-, p- in common names and 1,2 / 1,3 / 1,4 in IUPAC.
keyPoints: **Common name** = alkyl group + halide: CH₃CH₂Cl ethyl chloride, CH₃Br methyl bromide.
**IUPAC**: halogen as a **prefix** (fluoro, chloro, bromo, iodo); longest chain; number for the **lowest locants**: CH₃CH₂CH₂Br is **1-bromopropane**, not 3-.
**Tie → alphabetical order**: (CH₃)₂CHCH(Br)CH₃ gives {2,3} from both ends, so bromo gets 2: **2-bromo-3-methylbutane**.
**Haloarenes**: one X → same name (chlorobenzene); two X → **o-, m-, p-** = **1,2 / 1,3 / 1,4**.

sections.h: Common and IUPAC names side by side

list: Using alphabetical order before the lowest-locant rule: it only breaks a tie.
Writing a common name as the IUPAC name: ethyl bromide ✗, bromoethane ✓ (one word).
Reading meta as 1,4: meta is 1,3, para is 1,4.

quiz.q: The IUPAC name of isopropyl chloride, (CH3)2CHCl, is:
quiz.explain: Same compound: the common name says isopropyl + chloride; IUPAC numbers the propane chain and Cl sits on C2.

quiz.q: The common name of an alkyl halide is formed by:
options: the halo prefix followed by the alkane name
the alkyl group name followed by the halide name
the number of carbons followed by -ide
the halogen symbol followed by the alkane
quiz.explain: NCERT 6.2: alkyl group name, then the halide (ethyl chloride, methyl bromide).

quiz.q: In the IUPAC system, the halogen in an alkyl halide is written as:
options: a prefix such as chloro- or bromo- on the parent alkane
a separate word after the alkane
quiz.explain: IUPAC names halides as halo-substituted hydrocarbons, written as one word (bromoethane).

quiz.q: The IUPAC name of CH3CH2CH2Br is:
quiz.explain: Number from the end nearer Br: it gets locant 1, not 3.
Both ends give {2,3}: a tie, so bromo (B before M) gets the lower number, 2.

quiz.q: When both numbering directions give the same set of locants, the lower number goes to:
options: the substituent that comes first in alphabetical order
the substituent at the left end
quiz.explain: Alphabetical order only breaks a tie in the locants.

quiz.q: The common and IUPAC names of C6H5Cl are:
quiz.explain: One halogen on benzene: the common and IUPAC names are the same.

quiz.q: Which is an IUPAC name (not a common name)?
quiz.explain: Ethyl bromide, isopropyl chloride and methyl iodide are common names; bromoethane is IUPAC.

simulation.reason: Naming rules applied to fixed structures; no continuous variable to explore, and the video already counts the locants.
